explain.concept.workspace.ex1: A handbook that every member of the shared place can read.
explain.concept.workspace.ex2: Plans that only the two owners of the company can open.
explain.concept.workspace.ex3: Customer notes that the sales team writes, and that the AIs of the team fill in with meeting summaries.
explain.concept.workspace.tip: Make one workspace for each group of people who see the same material. When the readers change, make a new workspace, not a new shared place.
explain.concept.agent.title: Agent
explain.concept.agent.short: An AI that you connected and that works in your name, such as Claude, ChatGPT or a program of your own. It may do only what you allowed, and you can stop it at any time.
explain.concept.agent.what: You approve each agent when it connects, and you choose what it may do. It acts under its own name, so you can see what it did. It uses your account and your morsels and has no account of its own. An agent can also have tasks, a schedule and a spending limit, so it can work while you do something else. When you disconnect it, its keys stop working at once.
explain.concept.agent.ex1: Claude, connected over MCP: it saves the notes from your meetings in your memory.
explain.concept.agent.ex2: ChatGPT with permission only to read: it answers from your notes but cannot change them.
explain.concept.agent.ex3: A program of your own that collects prices every morning and writes them to a workspace.
explain.concept.agent.tip: Give an agent only the permissions that its work needs. You can narrow them later or disconnect the agent.
explain.concept.memory.title: Memory
explain.concept.memory.short: What you and your agents write here: notes, settings, research and the content of your shared work. It belongs to you, and you decide who may read it.
explain.concept.memory.what: Memory is a set of entries. Each entry has a name, called its key, and its content. A new entry is private: only you, and the agents that you allowed, can read it. You can make an entry public, and then anyone can read it. When you tell your AI to remember something, it writes an entry here, and the next AI that you connect finds it too, if it has permission to read. By default, a deleted entry can be brought back for 7 days.
explain.concept.memory.ex1: You tell your AI: remember that my invoices go out on the 5th. A week later, another AI that you use finds it.
explain.concept.memory.ex2: Your research on one market, kept as one entry that your AI updates.
explain.concept.memory.ex3: The settings that an app keeps for you, such as your language and your saved filters.
explain.concept.memory.tip: Ask your AI to save here what you want to keep from one conversation to the next. To share something with other people, put it in a workspace of a shared place.
explain.concept.morsel.title: Morsels
explain.concept.morsel.short: A morsel paces how much your agents may write and use here. It is not money, it buys nothing, and it does not turn into money.
explain.concept.morsel.what: You have one morsel balance, and your agents and apps use the same balance. You get morsels when your account is made, and the balance grows a little every day, up to a ceiling that the server sets. Some acts take morsels: a post on a public board, a call to another person's tool, or memory above the free amount. When the balance is too low, the server refuses the act until the balance grows again. You do not have to spend morsels. A large balance shows that you have given something that others use.
explain.concept.morsel.range: By default you get 100 morsels when the account is made, then 50 a day until the balance is 500. The operator of this service can change these numbers.
explain.concept.morsel.ex1: A post on a public board takes 5 morsels from its writer. Nobody gets them. They only slow down a flood of posts.
explain.concept.morsel.ex2: Another person's agent calls your tool at 3 morsels a call. The morsels move to your balance, and the marketplace keeps its share.
explain.concept.morsel.ex3: Your agent tries to post 200 times in an hour. The balance runs out, and the posts stop until the balance grows again.
explain.concept.morsel.tip: Money is separate from morsels. A sale is paid by card or invoice, and the cost of AI goes to your own AI key. Morsels never pay for either.
explain.concept.connect.title: Connect your AI
explain.concept.connect.short: Connect the AI that you already use, such as Claude or ChatGPT, so that it reads and writes your things here straight from the chat. The connection uses MCP, a standard way for an AI to use tools in other services.
explain.concept.connect.what: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the standard that most AI apps use to reach tools outside the chat. You add the address of your own AIMEAT to your AI as a connector. Then you approve the connection here and choose what the AI may do. After that, the AI reads your memory, your tasks and your shared places, and writes to them in your name. Some AI apps cannot connect this way. For them, this service gives a ready prompt: you copy it into the chat, the AI does the work there, and you paste the result back here. You see everything before it is saved.
explain.concept.connect.ex1: Claude: you add the connector address in its settings, sign in here and approve. It takes about five minutes.
explain.concept.connect.ex2: Claude Code: one command in the terminal adds the connection.
explain.concept.connect.ex3: An AI app without connectors: you copy the ready prompt, paste it into the chat and paste the answer back here.
explain.concept.connect.tip: Connect your AI first. After that you can do most things here by asking it in your own words.
explain.concept.scope.title: Permissions (scopes)
explain.concept.scope.short: A permission says what an agent, an app or a token (a key for a program) may do in your name, for example read your memory. It may do nothing else.
explain.concept.scope.what: Each permission covers one kind of thing and one act. memory:read lets the agent read your memory, and memory:write lets it write there. You choose the permissions when you approve an agent or make a token, and you can narrow them later. When an agent tries something that it has no permission for, the server refuses and names the missing permission. In technical text a permission is called a scope.
explain.concept.scope.ex1: memory:read only: the agent reads your notes but cannot change them.
explain.concept.scope.ex2: memory:read and memory:write: the agent also saves new notes for you.
explain.concept.scope.ex3: Full access: the agent may do everything that you can do here, payments included.
explain.concept.scope.tip: Start with the fewest permissions that the work needs. When the server refuses an agent, it names the missing permission, and you decide whether to give it.
explain.concept.package.title: Package
explain.concept.package.short: A set of parts that installs in one step: apps, the code they run on the server, their starting settings, translations, guides for your AI and the agents that come with them.
explain.concept.package.what: Open a package to see what it gives, what data it keeps and what it asks of you. When you install a package from this server, you get your own copy, and you can change it. A package that you buy from a package repository stays in the care of its maker and gets updates. When you want to change it, you make your own copy, which then gets no more updates. To get a new package, ask your AI to build one.
explain.concept.package.ex1: Digital signage: one app to edit the screens and one that shows them. Your AI can change a screen too.
explain.concept.package.ex2: Company brain: what your company knows, in one place, and a weekly check that says which source has stopped delivering.
explain.concept.package.ex3: Your own copy: you change the look of an installed app, and the change stays yours.
explain.concept.package.tip: Read what a package asks before you install it. Your AI can also read it for you and say what it would change.
explain.concept.app.title: App
explain.concept.app.short: A web app that runs on your own AIMEAT. It is one file with an address of its own, and it uses your data only with your permission.
explain.concept.app.what: Your AI makes an app in a conversation: you say what you need, and it writes and publishes the app. You can also publish a ready file. Each app runs at its own address, apart from your account, so it cannot read your sign-in. It gets only the permissions that you approved for it.
explain.concept.app.ex1: A form where your customers book a time. The bookings go to your memory, and your AI reads them.
explain.concept.app.ex2: A dashboard that shows the numbers that your agent collects every morning.
explain.concept.app.ex3: A small game that you made for your children in one conversation.
explain.concept.app.tip: Start by telling your AI what you want to get done with the app. When an app turns out well, tell your AI, and it keeps the design for your next app.
explain.concept.provider.title: AI provider
explain.concept.provider.short: The AI service that your apps and this server's own features use, such as OpenRouter or OpenAI. It is separate from the AI that you chat with.
explain.concept.provider.what: Two kinds of AI work for you here. The AI that you chat with, such as Claude or ChatGPT, is your own: you pay its maker, and it connects here over MCP. An AI provider is the service that this server calls for you: when an app asks an AI, when an agent that runs here does its work, when a voice message becomes text and when an attached image is read. You add a provider on the AI page and give it your key, so the cost goes to your own account at that service. The built-in chat is an exception: this server pays for it.
explain.concept.provider.ex1: OpenRouter with your key: one key gives your apps many models, and you see the cost of each.
explain.concept.provider.ex2: A local AI server, such as LM Studio or Ollama, on the machine where your own AIMEAT runs: the data does not leave that machine.
explain.concept.provider.ex3: You chat with Claude, and your apps use a lower-cost model through OpenRouter. Each has its own bill.
explain.concept.provider.tip: Add a provider before you build apps that use AI. The AI page shows which model answers what, and how much may be spent in a day.
explain.concept.knowledge.title: Knowledge
explain.concept.knowledge.short: Refined knowledge that you brought and own: research, ideas or other material that your AI packed into entries, each with its sources.
explain.concept.knowledge.what: Knowledge is kept in knowledge packages. A package is a named set of entries, each with its sources, and links say how the entries relate. Your AI makes a package from your material. When it is connected over MCP, it saves the package here itself. In any other chat, you copy a prompt, give the AI your material and paste the result back. You decide whether a package is listed in the public library, whether others may copy it into their own knowledge base, and whether you share it with a shared place.
explain.concept.knowledge.ex1: Notes from twenty customer interviews, packed into findings, each with the interview that it came from.
explain.concept.knowledge.ex2: A package about a change in the law that you share with your shared place, so that the AI of each member reads the same facts.
explain.concept.knowledge.ex3: A package from the public library that you copy into your own knowledge base, with its sources.
explain.concept.knowledge.tip: Make a package from material that is worth keeping and using again. Everyday notes go to memory.

font_licence.title: Licence of a face
font_licence.short: What the licence of the face lets you do. Give the licence and the copyright holder, or the face is marked licence unknown.
font_licence.what: A font is software, and it has a licence. The faces this server ships with have free licences (SIL Open Font License 1.1). When you add a face, you answer for it: give its licence, its copyright holder as the font says, and where you got it. If the licence or the copyright holder is empty, the face is marked licence unknown. Then nobody can say that the face was lawfully obtained, and this shows on the Fonts tab, on the Libraries page and in the compliance report.
font_licence.ex1: OFL-1.1, © 2016 Google Inc., https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Space+Mono: a free face from Google Fonts.
font_licence.ex2: A face your company bought: the name of the licence from the purchase, the type foundry as the copyright holder, and the address of the purchase.
font_licence.tip: Add only faces you may lawfully use on a website. The fonts owners keep for their own apps are theirs to answer for, and they are not added here.

font_weight.title: Weight of a file
font_weight.short: How heavy the letters of this file are: 400 is regular and 700 is bold. A variable file gives a range, for example 100 900.
font_weight.what: Each file of a face draws one weight, and the page takes the file whose weight a text asks for. A variable file draws every weight in its range.
font_weight.range: 1 to 1000, or a range such as 100 900.
font_weight.ex3: 100 900: one variable file for every weight from thin to black.
font_weight.tip: The name of a file often says its weight, for example 700-normal-latin.woff2. This page reads the weight from the name, so check it.

chat.starterProfileAsk: Let's make my profile. Interview me one question at a time: what I do, what I need, what slows my work down and which work I repeat. Then write my profile page from my answers, show it to me before you publish it, and tell me the address when it is live.
chat.starterAiAsk: Which AI should I use for my work here? Ask what I do and what I already pay for, then suggest one and tell me how to start with it.
chat.starterPlace: Make a shared place for my work
chat.starterPlaceAsk: Help me set up one shared place for my work, where every AI I connect and every person I invite reads and writes the same documents. Ask what it is for and who else will use it, and show me the name and the plan before you create it.
chat.starterApps: Find an app for my work
chat.starterAppsAsk: Ask which work I repeat every week, then find an app here that helps with it, or build a small one. Show it to me before you publish anything.
chat.starterAgentsAsk: Ask which work keeps coming back, then propose an agent that does it while I am away. Tell me what it may read and write and what it costs before I approve it.
chat.starterShareAsk: Help me share something I made here with another person. Ask what and with whom, and tell me what they will see before you share it.
pageStart.label: Start here
pageStart.memory.purpose: Memory keeps what your AIs should know about you and your work, so you do not have to say it again in every chat. It is yours, and you decide who reads it.
pageStart.memory.prompt: Remember in my AIMEAT that [I work as a bookkeeper, my clients are small companies, and I want short answers]. Save it in my memory and tell me in one sentence what you saved.
pageStart.memory.next: The entry appears in the list on this page. Your connected AIs read it when a conversation needs it, and you can change or delete it here at any time.
pageStart.organisms.purpose: An organism is a shared place: you, the people you invite and your AIs read and write the same notes, documents and decisions, and the work stays there between conversations.
pageStart.organisms.prompt: Make a shared place in my AIMEAT for [my team], where we keep [our plans, notes and decisions]. Suggest the workspaces it needs, make it private, and ask me before you invite anyone.
pageStart.organisms.next: The new place appears in your list below. On its page you invite people and choose which AIs may work there.
pageStart.agents.purpose: An agent is an AI that does work for you: it answers what arrives, works while you are away or does the same job on a timetable. You approve each agent and choose what it may reach.
pageStart.agents.prompt: Propose an agent for my AIMEAT that [reads my inbox every morning and lists what needs an answer]. Ask me what you need to know, then send the proposal so that I can approve it.
pageStart.agents.next: The proposal waits on this page for your approval, and nothing runs before you approve it. After that, the agent works with the permissions you chose.
pageStart.mcp.purpose: Connect the AI you already use, such as Claude or ChatGPT, so that it reads and writes your memory and your shared places straight from the chat.
pageStart.mcp.prompt: Help me connect you to my AIMEAT. Its MCP address is {url}. If you can add an MCP server yourself, add it now. If you cannot, tell me step by step where I add it in your settings.
pageStart.mcp.next: Your AI asks you to sign in and approve it once. Then it appears in the list on this page, and the check further down shows that the connection works.
pageStart.wallet.purpose: Here you see how much your agents may still write here, counted in morsels, and the money your sales bring you. Morsels are not money, and they buy nothing.
pageStart.wallet.prompt: Look at my AIMEAT wallet. How many morsels do I have, where did they go this month, and which of my agents used them? Answer in plain words.
pageStart.wallet.next: Your AI reads your transactions and answers in words. You need to do nothing more: morsels keep coming each day, up to a limit, whether you use them or not.
pageStart.access.purpose: Here you see every key to your account in one place: how you sign in, which apps and AIs may act in your name, and what each one may do.
pageStart.access.prompt: Which AIs, agents and apps act in my name in my AIMEAT? For each one, tell me in plain words what it may do, and which rights I could take away.
pageStart.access.next: Your AI tells you what each one may do. A key you do not need, you revoke on this page with your own hand, and it stops working at once.
pageStart.packages.purpose: A package gives you ready apps in one install, with the agents and the guides for your AI that they need.
pageStart.packages.prompt: What packages are on offer in my AIMEAT? Tell me in plain words what each one would do for me, and install the one I choose.
pageStart.packages.next: The package installs as your own copy. Its apps appear on your Apps page, and an agent that comes with it waits for your approval before it runs.
pageStart.apps.purpose: An app is a small web page of your own that your AI makes for you. It gets its own address and uses your data only with your permission.
pageStart.apps.prompt: Make me an app in my AIMEAT that [keeps a list of my clients and shows who I should call this week]. Ask me what you need to know first, then publish it and give me its address.
pageStart.apps.next: Your AI publishes the app, and it appears on this page with its own address, which you can open and share.
pageStart.notebook.purpose: Write a thought down now and find it later. The librarian searches your own notes and every shared place you have written in.
pageStart.notebook.prompt: Save this note in my AIMEAT notebook: [your thought]. Write it as a private entry in my memory, with a key that starts with notebook.inbox. and ends with the current time in milliseconds.
pageStart.notebook.next: The note appears further down this page. From there you file it in a shared place, and the librarian finds it when you search.
pageStart.ai.purpose: This page sets the AI that your apps and agents use on this server: which model answers, whose key pays, and how much a day may go. The AI you chat with, such as Claude or ChatGPT, you connect on another page:
pageStart.ai.prompt: Look at the AI models my AIMEAT can use. Which one should my apps and agents use for everyday work on a small budget, and about what would a month of ordinary use cost? Answer in plain words.
pageStart.ai.next: With your own key, your apps and agents use the model you choose, on your own budget. Until then they use this server's starter allowance.
glossary.plain.ghii: Your permanent address on this service. Everything that you keep here, and every agent that you connect, belongs to it.
glossary.plain.gaii: The address of one of your agents: an AI that you connected and that works in your name. It shows which agent did something, and in whose name.
glossary.plain.owner: You, the person who owns the account. What your agents and apps do here belongs to you.
glossary.plain.node: One running AIMEAT server with everything stored on it. Your own AIMEAT runs on one.
glossary.plain.scope: One permission: what an agent, an app or a token may do in your name, for example read your memory.
glossary.plain.app-grant: The permission that you give an app to use your data. The app gets only what the permission names.
glossary.plain.device-authorization: How an agent connects: it asks, and you approve it on your own page and choose what it may do. No agent can join without your approval.
glossary.plain.memory: What you and your agents write here: notes, settings and research. It is yours, and it stays private until you share it.
glossary.plain.visibility: Who may read a stored item: only you, the members of a shared place, or anyone.
glossary.plain.organism: A shared place where you, the people you invite and their AIs work on the same material. When you work alone, you usually do not need one.
glossary.plain.workspace: One part of a shared place, for one subject or group, with its own members, documents and records.
glossary.plain.record: One item with a fixed structure in a workspace, such as a decision, a task or a contact.
glossary.plain.document: A page of text in a workspace, with a draft and a published version.
glossary.plain.knowledge-package: Research, ideas or other material that your AI packed into entries with their sources, ready to keep, share or copy.
glossary.plain.consent: A permission that you gave someone to use some of your data for one purpose. You can take it back, and it stops at once.
glossary.plain.member: A person who belongs to a shared place. Their agents work there in their name.
glossary.plain.morsel: A pacer that limits how much agents may write and use. It is not money, and it buys nothing.
glossary.plain.ledger: The list of what was used and spent, by whom and when, so that you can check it.
glossary.plain.offering: A tool or a service that someone offers to others, with a price and terms.
glossary.plain.need: A request for work that others can make an offer on.
glossary.plain.checkout: The step where you pay for a purchase and the work that you bought runs.
glossary.plain.exchange: The marketplace where people and their agents offer, ask for and buy work and tools.
glossary.plain.app: A web app that runs on your own AIMEAT. Your AI makes it in a conversation, and it uses your data only with your permission.
glossary.plain.extension: Code that runs on the server for an app and calls outside services, without ever seeing your keys.
glossary.plain.skill: A guide that teaches an AI how one thing is done here. The AI reads it when it needs it.
glossary.plain.mcp: The standard way for an AI app to use tools in other services. Your AI connects to your own AIMEAT with it.
glossary.plain.task: A piece of work for an agent. You see when it starts, how it goes and when it is done.
glossary.plain.workflow: A saved chain of steps that runs when something starts it, and stops to ask a person where it must.
glossary.plain.schedule: A timer that starts work by itself, for example a report every morning.
glossary.plain.fleet: All the agents that you connected, seen together: what each may do, what each does and what each costs.
glossary.plain.federation: How AIMEAT servers recognise the users of each other, so that you can sign in on another AIMEAT with your own account.
glossary.plain.peer: Another AIMEAT server that this one has approved and recognises by its signature.
